studyArea: 2024 Remington Wildfire & Southern Montana / Northern Wyoming Powder River Basin
coreQuestion: Do surface vegetation wildfires generate new, persistent coal-seam fires, which can subsequently reignite surface vegetation?

datasets.name: 2024 Remington Wildfire Final Perimeter (WFIGS)
datasets.publisher: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) / Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services (WFIGS)
datasets.limitations: Represents the final cumulative surface wildfire footprint (196,368.1 acres; polygon snapshot poly_PolygonDateTime 2025-01-15). Does not provide daily progression perimeters, internal unburned island high-resolution burn severity, or subsurface thermal measurements.

dataGapsChecklist.category: Verified Post-2024 Subsurface Coal-Fire Point Inventory
dataGapsChecklist.sourcesChecked: NIFC WFIGS, MT DNRC, BLM Montana/Dakotas Public GIS, MBMG Open-File Catalog, USGS ScienceBase (checked 2026-09-24).
dataGapsChecklist.scientificImpact: Default real-data mode contains 1 official wildfire perimeter and 0 verified coal-fire point observations. Secondary reporting (Montana Free Press, Sept 2025) describes 107 burning seams mapped after the Remington fire, and a Feb 2026 Montana DES mapping bulletin is noted as a primary-source lead, but no public coordinate inventory with precision and pre-fire baseline metadata has been acquired.

dataGapsChecklist.category: Source-Backed Local Clinker & Coal Outcrop Vector Layer
dataGapsChecklist.status: NOT ACQUIRED IN REPOSITORY (Schematic Fixture Quarantined)
dataGapsChecklist.sourcesChecked: USGS Professional Paper 1625-A & MBMG regional stratigraphy catalogs (checked 2026-09-24).
dataGapsChecklist.scientificImpact: No survey-grade digitized coal outcrop or clinker polygon layer is currently bundled. Hand-drawn schematic polygons are quarantined behind the Synthetic Validation Fixtures toggle so they cannot be mistaken for observed geology.

dataGapsChecklist.category: Pre-Fire vs. Post-Fire Thermal Baseline (Before August 22, 2024)
dataGapsChecklist.status: MISSING SYSTEMATIC BASELINE IN ACQUIRED DATA
dataGapsChecklist.sourcesChecked: LANDFIRE, USGS Coal Fields of the Conterminous US, Heffern & Coates (2004) synthesis.
dataGapsChecklist.scientificImpact: First post-fire detection of a smoldering seam cannot be equated with new ignition by the 2024 Remington Wildfire unless pre-fire absence or new ignition mechanism is independently established.

dataGapsChecklist.sourcesChecked: Geophysical coal-fire literature (borehole thermometry, electrical resistivity, UAV FLIR).
dataGapsChecklist.scientificImpact: Multiple surface fumaroles along a clinker bench may stem from a single continuous underground combustion zone; treating individual vents as independent ignitions inflates fire counts.

remingtonCaseChronology.title: 2024 Remington Wildfire & Post-Fire Coal Seam Activity — Source-Linked Evidence Matrix
remingtonCaseChronology.purpose: Distinguishes what the official 2024–2025 geospatial record establishes from attributed secondary reporting, unacquired primary survey inventories, and separate regional hydrology literature.

entries.claimOrObservation: Remington Wildfire discovery timestamp (attr_FireDiscoveryDateTime) in Sheridan County, WY, burning northward into Big Horn, Rosebud, and Powder River Counties, MT. Reported general/specific cause in WFIGS: Natural / Lightning (attr_IsFireCauseInvestigated: 0).
entries.reportedPostfireCoalActivity: Not recorded in WFIGS perimeter attributes.
entries.surveyCoverageStatus: Final cumulative perimeter only (196,368.1 GIS acres); no daily progression series in repository.
entries.prefireBaselineStatus: No pre-August 2024 coal-seam thermal baseline included in WFIGS.

entries.claimOrObservation: WFIGS records containment on 2024-09-21, control on 2024-11-12, and final polygon snapshot timestamp (poly_PolygonDateTime) on 2025-01-15.

entries.mappedPerimeterDate: Unpublished in public GIS (non-spatial narrative lead)
entries.claimOrObservation: Montana Free Press (reporter Leigh Walden, Sept 2025) reported that local/agency post-fire mapping identified 107 burning coal seams in connection with the 2024 Remington Wildfire scar.
entries.reportedPostfireCoalActivity: Attributed report of '107 burning seams' mapped after the 2024 Remington fire. Treated strictly as an attributed secondary lead — NOT a verified point inventory or a count of newly ignited independent subsurface combustion bodies until traced to primary survey records.
entries.surveyCoverageStatus: Underlying GPS/IR survey tracklines, detection thresholds, and negative-survey boundaries have not been published in public GIS repositories.
entries.prefireBaselineStatus: UNRESOLVED: Public reporting does not establish how many of the 107 mapped thermal features were newly ignited by August 2024 surface wildfire pass-over versus pre-existing smoldering seams exposed or noticed during post-fire inspections.
entries.groupingUncertainty: UNRESOLVED MULTI-VENT AMBIGUITY: Without the primary survey protocol, it is unknown whether '107' counts individual surface smoke/heat vents along shared coal outcrops or 107 physically independent subsurface combustion bodies.
entries.sourceCitation: Leigh Walden, Montana Free Press (September 2025 reporting on post-Remington coal seam fires)

entries.claimOrObservation: February 2026 Montana Disaster and Emergency Services (MT DES) / county coal-seam mapping bulletin identified as a primary-source follow-up lead to verify survey holder metadata, coordinates, and detection methodology behind post-Remington coal-fire counts.
entries.reportedPostfireCoalActivity: Primary GIS point/polygon inventory and attribute table not acquired in local repository as of Sept 2026.
entries.surveyCoverageStatus: Pending primary agency data acquisition; rendered as non-spatial lead only.
entries.prefireBaselineStatus: Requires cross-checking against pre-2024 MBMG/BLM outcrop fire records.
entries.groupingUncertainty: Pending primary survey attribute definitions (individual fumaroles vs. seam complexes).
entries.sourceCitation: Montana DES / County Emergency Management Mapping Bulletin Lead (Feb 2026)

hydrologyContextNote.citation: Meredith, E. (2016). Coal aquifer contribution to streams in the Powder River Basin, Montana. Journal of Hydrology / MBMG.
hydrologyContextNote.relevance: Establishes water-isotope and strontium-isotope methods for quantifying coal-bed aquifer baseflow contributions to Powder River Basin streams (including Rosebud Creek, Tongue River, and Otter Creek).
hydrologyContextNote.epistemicLimitation: SEPARATE RESEARCH BRANCH: Meredith (2016) traces natural coal-aquifer groundwater contribution to streams, NOT active coal-fire combustion contaminant plumes or post-wildfire ash runoff. PRBsim intentionally does NOT render groundwater contamination zones or hydrological plume polygons from coal-bearing stratigraphy.
